exercise.name: Leg Over Knee Glute Bridge

reference.title: Leg Over Knee Glute Bridge (male)
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.laterality: Unilateral (right leg works; left ankle crossed over the right knee)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you drive up through the planted heel, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, 1 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.progression: Longer squeeze, then single-leg bridge with the free leg straight, then single-leg hip thrust

cues.text: Lie on your back, right foot flat, left ankle crossed over the right knee (figure 4), arms by your sides.
Breathe out, press through the right heel and drive the hips up.
Knee, hip and shoulder in one line; keep the pelvis level, do not let the crossed side drop.
Touch down lightly, repeat, then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Pelvis dropping or twisting toward the crossed leg
mistakes.fix: Brace and squeeze the working glute; keep both hip bones level.
Drive through the heel of the planted foot.
Ribs down, stop at a straight line.
Rest the outer ankle just above the knee on the thigh.

kinematics.norm: Working hip extends to about neutral at the top (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees on the working leg at the top (Lehecka 2017 traditional bridge position)
Outer ankle rests on the thigh just above the knee; the crossed hip turns out (clinical opinion)
Pelvis lifts until the working knee, hip and shoulder line up (clinical opinion)
About 1.5 s up, a 1 s squeeze, 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #10854, Leg Over Knee Glute Bridge (male) (movement reference only)
Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)
Electromyographic analysis of core trunk, hip and thigh muscles during 9 rehabilitation exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2007; PubMed 18560185)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Hip or knee discomfort in the crossed position: uncross and do a single-leg bridge with the free knee held up.
Low back discomfort: lift less high and brace first.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Too hard: both feet down (glute bridge) with the crossed leg resting lightly.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Main target: lifts the pelvis on one leg; single-leg bridging is one of the higher gluteus maximus exercises (Ekstrom 2007; Boren 2011).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension on the working side.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg (Boren 2011 ranked single-leg bridging high for gluteus medius).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Stop the crossed side from dropping.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Stop the crossed side from dropping.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk straight without over-arching.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk straight without over-arching.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Lengthened by the figure-4 crossed position.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Lengthened by the figure-4 crossed position.

guides.label: Hips drive up on the right leg
Working hip extended to neutral at the top
